beta_new: Follow the obvious crack through a bulge about 20 feet up, keep going to the rappel anchors above Pony Express, then trend up and right on cracks and buckets to the top.
Follow twin cracks and a corner up to a bolted belay stance. From there, traverse down-left along the crack, then ascend leftward to finish.
Starting on the ledge above the neighboring route, clip a bolt and move into a crack that curves rightward.
Begin just right of its neighbor, climbing huecos first, then move onto smoother rock above where three bolts protect.
Begin on the neighboring route, then after clipping its first bolt, veer rightward over a roof.

moves.from: ; a couple of small cams are worth bringing

beta_new: Sustained slightly overhanging climbing on pockets and pinches, clipping eight bolts up to the anchor.
Begin around the corner to the right, use buckets to cross the neighboring crack, then proceed vertically past three bolts.
Clip the lone bolt low down, then follow the crack closest to the dark streaks on their left.
A tree anchor at the top allows toproping, but expect a long swing if you fall before reaching the crack.
Begin on a ramp tending left, work leftward, then ascend a crack with three bolts for protection.
A Sidewinder variation: take the wall higher up and to the right of its arched crack, and merge back into it at the final bolt.
Follow the obvious dike that slants rightward, clipping four bolts along the way.
Follow the dike as it slants leftward, clipping two bolts.

Leave the ledge to the right of the neighboring route and head up and a bit leftward, clipping four bolts before reaching a stance where you may belay.

Clip a single additional bolt higher up; the crux is height-dependent.
Skip the hard dihedral start by going up and left to the little buttress forming the foot of the Southeast Face route, then cross rightward over shallow ledges to the dihedral.
Begin at the foot of Damper and angle up leftward to a flake; the crux step off it gets protection from a drilled angle.
Usually toproped; leading it is possible but the top offers little protection.
Begin in the wide crack of a right-facing corner, move rightward to clip a bolt, then ascend a seam clipping four more.

moves.from: clip a bolt, then ascend a seam clipping four more

beta_new: Take the curving chimney beside its neighbor up to a ledge belay, then follow the crack until it ends and shift leftward to finish by an aging bolt.
Begin well over from Panther Crack, layback a crack in a left-facing corner, then continue on the face, clipping two bolts plus a questionable fixed pin.
Work up discontinuous cracks, passing an old bolt, to reach the ledge, then continue in the chimney above.
Begin a bit beyond Gorgasaurus with bouldery moves up a seam, shift right past two bolts, then head up and right to join Negasaurus at its last crack.
Get through the loose rock low down; the climbing turns steep and dynamic once the final headwall is reached. Pass the first bolt, then finish rightward onto the overhanging headwall.
Traversing in from the right at the level of bolt two turns it into a much easier outing.
Begin in the corner beside the pine and follow the three bolts straight to the top.
The upper part follows a beautiful arete; a bolt added in the gap above bolt two now removes what used to be a runout.
Follow the thin crack as it tends leftward; at the bolt atop it, step right and merge with the neighboring route's final bolt.
Share the opening thin crack with the neighboring route, then head straight up, clipping three bolts.
Link the three bolts as they ascend the steep, sustained wall.
Follow Midnight Lumber to about mid-height, then traverse rightward along the dike with four bolts and finish up the top of The Woodshed.
The first pitch is short, linking a trio of solid bolts plus a couple of old ones, ending in a small cave holding the first anchors.
Follow four bolts up a face covered with patina plates.
Ascend the north face with three bolts; after the third, trend left, then angle back right to the top.
Drop-knee rests and a fist jam can help, and a dynamic lunge is the alternative; leading is avoided because protection stops when the crack does.
Above the bolt past the small ledge, step rightward to merge with the neighboring line.
Begin inside the chimney to the right, angle leftward by one bolt to reach the horizontal dike, traverse it left clipping two bolts, then finish upward with three more bolts.
Begin next to the neighboring route, get by a decayed flake, then angle rightward along a dike to the face with two bolts.
Begin five feet right of the neighboring route, follow its crack until it ends, then move up the face with two bolts.
Launch off the right-hand tip of Bat Ledge, surmount a bulge, then continue up the face beside Southwest Passage's upper pitch, clipping three bolts.
Begin on the flake shared with the previous route, then head straight upward clipping three bolts.
